findings.classification: newly identified inherited cleanup defect; source is untracked relative to HEAD, so earlier build-tools report/source lineage is the comparison, not a claimed committed regression
findings.title: Failed cleanup is permanently marked complete enough to skip the final attempt
findings.impact: A transient ps failure after SIGSTOP leaves the worker frozen and alive. run records failure then its finally calls stop_worker again, which immediately returns because breezer_cleanup_attempted is already true. Detached compiler groups can likewise remain alive if discovery or later termination fails. No retry of the build occurs, but cleanup is incomplete.
findings.reachability: Stop or worker-exit handling calls stop_worker. process_table uses check_output and parsing, either of which can raise; failure is not caught inside cleanup. The fake reproduces the first discovery failure after the actual SIGSTOP branch. No claim of a PC incident.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B build/efficiency-20261103/build-current-audit-probe.py; cleanupRetryFailure: two calls produce one process_table call and only SIGSTOP, child remains live. OS/process functions are fake and no workers were started.
findings.smallestFix: Mark successful cleanup only after reaping and final survivor verification. Keep failed cleanup retryable, preserve discovered ownership for retries, and ensure an exception after freezing cannot leave the worker stopped without a bounded terminate/resume fallback. Add a fake transient discovery failure followed by successful cleanup test. Do not weaken ownership checks.
